decisions: alexei-led/ccgram rejected at sighting 3 rather than listed, resolving the Herdr-specificity question the 2026-08-29 audit deferred to this point. Opening it settled it: CCGram sits on top of a terminal multiplexer and names three interchangeable backends — tmux, Herdr, and agterm — so Herdr is a backend, not the purpose, and the project would be as useful with Herdr removed. The Herdr integration is real and deep (socket protocols 14-20, agent.list as the sole identity source, opaque herdr-session-v1 targets), which is why it survived two sightings, and it fails on specificity alone at 262 stars and MIT. Rejected alternative: listing it in Phone and mobile, where five Herdr-only clients already cover the ground.

'Remote and mobile' split into 'Remote access' and 'Phone and mobile' rather than retiring a healthy incumbent. The five promotions would have taken the section to 9 against a soft cap of 8, and the cap rule offers splitting or replacing; every incumbent still clears every bar, so retiring one to make room would have been churn. The split is functional — reaching a server from another computer, versus driving agents from a phone — and leaves both sections well under the cap.

jhochenbaum/herdr-hunk-diff listed despite the overlap flag against herdr-reviewr raised at sighting 1. They are close but not the same job: reviewr is a general review-and-file-viewer sidebar, hunk-diff is hunk-granular diff review with inline comments routed back to the authoring agent. Rejected alternative: replacing reviewr, which has 625 stars and is healthy on every measure. The section sits at 4 of 8, so both fit; re-examine if either stalls.

decisions: Sightings not advanced and nothing promoted, because this run fell 4 days after the 2026-09-08 audit. AGENTS.md specifies a three-week probation and the skill says nothing reaches the list in under three weeks; sightings are weekly checkpoints, not per-run counters — the three runs dated 2026-08-12 are the in-ledger precedent, and none of them advanced anything. Advancing would have taken all 14 entries first seen 2026-08-29 to sighting 3 and into the README 14 days after first sight, 11 days after the previous batch of 11 listings, pushing Extras and Phone and mobile past the soft cap. Rejected alternative: treat each run as a sighting. The cost of holding is a few days; the 2026-08-29 cohort reaches three weeks on 2026-09-19 and the 2026-09-08 cohort on 2026-09-29. Note for the next scheduled run on 2026-09-14: that is still under three weeks for the 2026-08-29 cohort, so the same reasoning holds there.

AltanS/collie kept listed despite now supporting tmux and zellij as well as Herdr — the same pattern that got alexei-led/ccgram rejected at sighting 3 on 2026-09-08. The difference is asymmetry: ccgram names Herdr as one of three interchangeable backends, while Collie's README states 'Herdr is the primary supported target in 1.0' and calls tmux and zellij experimental, tested by a single operator on one machine; its description and topics still say Herdr. It has not fallen below the bar, so per Phase 1 this is CHANGED, not probation. Rejected alternative: probation for specificity, which would treat an experimental side-backend as a change of purpose. Re-check every audit: if tmux or zellij leave experimental, it fails the same test ccgram failed.

missuo/herdrm re-promoted from rejected to candidate at sighting 1 after adopting PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0 on 2026-09-10, following the 2026-08-29 precedent for pi-bellwether and herdr-nvim. The documented bar requires a license, not an open-source one, so it qualifies as written. But noncommercial terms forbid most at-work use, and that is a policy question this audit should not settle alone: flagged for human confirmation before it could reach sighting 3 (earliest 2026-10-03), and any eventual entry must say 'noncommercial use only' the way whip flags AGPL. Rejected alternative: keep it rejected as an incompatible license — the bar does not define incompatible, and inventing that rule mid-audit would be the kind of silent policy change the protocol exists to prevent.

jerryfane/herdrup rejected at first sighting despite 124 stars and Apache-2.0: its README says it needs jerryfane/herdr, a 6-star fork of the runtime that adds the gram, push, and live-terminal APIs. A client that does not do its job against Herdr as shipped is not a Herdr client for this list's readers. Rejected alternative: candidate with a flag, which would carry it for three weeks against a blocker the author states outright. It re-enters from candidate if those APIs land upstream.

Trending: the 2026-09-08 seed item replaces the 2026-08-06 Y Combinator item rather than evicting a different one to stay at the cap of 8. The seed post is the continuation of the YC post (it opens by referring back to it) and names Y Combinator among its investors. Rejected alternative: dropping the v0.8.2 release item, which still carries the Windows GA news that v0.9.0 does not restate.

New rejects: jerryfane/herdrup (fork dependency), ThorstenRhau/token and ogulcancelik/pi-extensions (not Herdr-specific), and 10 articles failing the first-hand bar (bitdoze, developersdigest, dotzlaw, chaseai, akmatori, shareuhack, genztech, opentechhub, intelligentliving, coddykit) — recorded so they are not re-read from scratch. sources.last_change: 2026-09-08: sighting 3 reached; the deferred Herdr-specificity decision resolved as a reject.
sources.notes: Carried to sighting 3 as borderline, then rejected 2026-09-08 on the Herdr-specific bar. Opened this run: CCGram is a Telegram bridge that sits on top of a terminal multiplexer and names three interchangeable backends — tmux, Herdr, and agterm — so Herdr is a backend rather than the purpose. The Herdr integration is genuinely deep (socket protocols 14-20, agent.list as the sole identity source, opaque herdr-session-v1 targets, `herdr integration install`), which is why it survived two sightings, but the project would be exactly as useful with Herdr removed. 262 stars, MIT, pushed 2026-09-05 — it fails on specificity alone, not traction. Rejected alternative: listing it in Phone and mobile, which the four Herdr-only clients already cover. Re-open only if it becomes Herdr-first.

sources.notes: Sighting 1 of 3. Thin wrapper opening Yazi in a Herdr split or tab at the triggering pane's directory. Exactly at the 25-star bar. sources.title: weawr

evidence.method: GitHub API 2026-09-12; README read; adapters directory listed

sources.notes: Sighting 1 of 3. Team and coordination layer on top of Herdr: watches an issue tracker, runs each assignment as a Herdr workspace, and lets agents nudge each other through Herdr's API. Herdr is its only multiplexer adapter (packages/engine/src/adapters/herdr.mjs). Found via yigitkonur/awesome-herdr, not the herdr topics. Created 2026-09-05 — one week old.

sources.title: herdrup

evidence.method: GitHub API 2026-09-12; README read; jerryfane/herdr confirmed as a fork of herdrdev/herdr via GitHub API

sources.notes: Rejected at first sighting: requires a fork of the runtime. iOS client (App Store) with a status board, live terminal, and agent messaging, 124 stars and Apache-2.0 — but its README says you need jerryfane/herdr, a 6-star fork of herdrdev/herdr that adds the gram, push, and live-terminal APIs, and the app warns when talking to a daemon without them. Not usable as intended against Herdr as shipped. Re-evaluate from candidate if those APIs land upstream or the fork requirement goes away.

trending_policy: Trending items are exempt from the probation rule and are NOT sources: they are dated, sourced news items dropped after ~8 weeks or when superseded. A trending item never graduates into `sources` automatically — an entry must clear the normal bar on its own.

trending.text: Herdr raised a $6M seed led by Bessemer Venture Partners, with Y Combinator, e2vc, and angels including Tobi Lütke (Shopify), Dane Knecht (Cloudflare), and Görkem Yurtseven (fal). The runtime stays open, the money goes to hiring, and applications go through an SSH endpoint instead of a web form. Supersedes the 2026-08-06 Y Combinator item.

v0.9.0 removes the single-process `--no-session` mode: every TUI launch now attaches to a background server, and `server stop` is what ends a session. Closing a primary workspace that has open worktree workspaces now needs explicit group intent (`workspace close --group`), and new lifecycle event subscriptions start with live events instead of replaying retained history — API and plugin clients must subscribe before taking their initial snapshot or they will miss changes.

v0.9.0: local and saved SSH machines now live in one window with a combined agent list and automatic reconnects (`herdr machine`), multiple clients can view different workspaces and tabs independently, the terminal UI moved into each client to cut redraw work in busy multi-client sessions, and Kitty graphics are on by default in compatible terminals.
Blog: 'Connecting the machines' — the 0.9 multi-machine client, why it took longer than expected, and Herdr Cloud named as what comes next.

v0.8.2: Windows support is now generally available on stable (previously preview-only); the plugin marketplace now discovers manifests at repository roots and subdirectories and groups multiple plugins per repository; Qwen Code state detection and native session restore.
Blog: 'Ten agents, three clients, 95% less CPU' — rendering and status-indicator work for running a fleet.

37,992 stars on 2026-09-12, up from 36,426 four days earlier and ~15k in early July, when it hit #1 on GitHub Trending; the 0.9 announcement put downloads above 700,000. The plugin marketplace held 1,130 repositories on the same date, up from 1,033; 65 of them clear this list's 25-star bar, up from 60.
No company publicly documented as running Herdr in production could be found. Standing search target.
